Question
========


Streudiagramme (scatterplots) zeigen den Zusammenhang zweier numerischer Variablen auf; die Stärke des Zusammenhangs lässt sich per Augenschein abschätzen.

Das folgende Diagramm zeigt lineare Zusammenhänge der Stärke Null, schwach, mittel, stark und perfekt. Außerdem sind gleichsinnige (positive) und gegensinnige (negative) Zusammenhänge dargestellt sowie der Null-Zusammenhang.


```{r}
kv_pair <- tibble::tribble(
  ~key, ~value,
   "A",     -1,
   "B",   -0.9,
   "C",  -0.75,
   "D",   -0.3,
   "E",      0,
   "F",    0.3,
   "G",   0.75,
   "H",    0.9,
   "I",      1
  )


```






```{r}
#### Quelle http://moderndive.com/scripts/06-regression.R
## Leichte Anpassungen durch N. Markgraf
# library(mosaic)
library(mvtnorm) 
set.seed(2009)

correlation <- c(-0.999999, -0.90, -0.75, -0.30, 0.00, 0.30, 0.75, 0.90, 0.999999)
eps <- 0.00001
n_sim <- 100

values <- NULL
for (i in 1:length(correlation)) {
    rho <- correlation[i]
    rs <- rho * sqrt(50)
    sigma <- matrix(c(5, rs, rs, 10), 2, 2) 
    sim <- rmvnorm(
        n = n_sim,
        mean = c(20,40),
        sigma = sigma
    )
    r <- cor(sim[,1],sim[,2])
    new_err <- NULL
    new_r <- NULL
    err <- abs(rho - r)
    for (j in 1:1000) {
        sim_t <- rmvnorm(
            n = n_sim,
            mean = c(20,40),
            sigma = sigma
        )
        new_r <- cor(sim_t[,1], sim_t[,2])
        new_err <- abs(rho - new_r)
        if (new_err < err) {
            # cat(paste("want:",rho,"- got:",r,"- err:",err,"- new:",new_r,"new-err:",new_err,"\n"))
            sim <- sim_t
            r <- new_r
            err <- new_err
        }
        if (new_err < eps) {
            break
        }
    }
    sim %>%   
        as.data.frame() %>% 
        mutate(correlation = round(rho,2)) %>%
        mutate(reel_correlation = round(cor(V1,V2),2)) %>%
        mutate(reel_correlation_2 = round(r,2)) %>%
        mutate(cor_err = err) -> sim
    
    values <- bind_rows(values, sim)
}


detach("package:mvtnorm", unload=TRUE)
```



```{r join-corr-id}

values2 <-
  values %>% 
  full_join(kv_pair, by = c("correlation" = "value"))
```


```{r join-corr-types}
corr_types <- 
  tibble::tribble(
     ~Staerke,      ~Richtung, ~correlation,
    "schwach", "gleichsinnig",          0.3,
    "schwach",  "gegensinnig",         -0.3,
     "mittel", "gleichsinnig",         0.75,
     "mittel",  "gegensinnig",        -0.75,
      "stark", "gleichsinnig",          0.9,
      "stark",  "gegensinnig",         -0.9,
    "perfekt", "gleichsinnig",            1,
    "perfekt",  "gegensinnig",           -1,
       "null",         "null",            0
    )



corr_types_id <-
  kv_pair %>% 
  full_join(corr_types, by = c("value" = "correlation"))

```





```{r plot-diagram}

ggplot(data = values2, mapping = aes(V1, V2)) +
```

Gesucht ist das Diagramm, das folgende Art von Zusammenhang zeigt:

```{r create-item-list}
selected_id <- sample(c(T, rep(F, times = 8)), size = 9)

corr_types_id2 <-
  corr_types_id %>% 
  mutate(selected_id = selected_id)


items <- 
  corr_types_id2 %>% 
  sample_n(size = nrow(.)) %>% 
  filter(selected_id != TRUE) %>% 
  slice(1:4) %>% 
  bind_rows(corr_types_id2 %>% filter(selected_id == TRUE))

items %>% 
  filter(selected_id == TRUE) %>% 
  select(Staerke, Richtung) %>% 
  kbl() %>% 
  kable_classic(full_width = F, html_font = "Cambria")

```




```{r questionlist, results="asis"}
exams::answerlist(items$key, 
           markup = "markdown")
```



Solution
========


Aufgabenname: `scatterplot-art-korrelation`


```{r, echo = FALSE, results = "asis"}
exams::answerlist(ifelse(items$selected_id, "Richtig", "Falsch"), markup = "markdown")
```
